title: Throughput Assurance Addendum: Multi-dimensional SLOs, Rolling Error Budget, and Customer Remedy Matrix
creator: Nora Chen
description: Background: Enterprise customers purchasing Redwood Dedicated ask for clear, auditable throughput guarantees tied to predictable crediting when commitments are missed. Existing SLA drafts focus on single-dimension throughput (tokens/minute) and bulk credit formulas that are difficult to reconcile with autoscale/autoremediation behavior. This ticket defines a multi-dimensional throughput assurance addendum that: 1) specifies measurable SLOs across throughput, tail-latency during contention, and sustained burst handling; 2) introduces a rolling error-budget model (sliding 30-day window) that aligns with autoscaler triggers; and 3) provides plain-language contract clauses for credit computation, notice, and remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: - Legal has approved the plain-language clauses and signature-ready appendix. - Measurement spec implements the three SLOs in telemetry with dashboard and automated daily reports. - Billing/finance has validated example credit computations for three customer profiles. - One pilot customer (existing Dedicated tenant) signs an early addendum for evaluation. - Dev/Eng has implemented the alerting hooks to tie autoscaler state to error-budget burn metrics.
proposed_contract_clauses: 1) Definitions: 'Committed Throughput' (CT) = customer reserved TPS-equivalent measured as tokens-per-minute averaged over 5-minute windows at the ingress front-door; 'Sustained Band' = percentage of CT sustained for 15+ minutes without autoscale intervention; 'Degradation Window' = any contiguous 5-minute interval where measured throughput < 90% of CT. 2) SLA Objective: Redwood guarantees that across a rolling 30-day period, measured CT attainment >= 99.5% of customer CT quota (see measurement spec). 3) Error Budget & Credits: For each 30-day window, compute shortfall S = max(0, CT*30days - observed_served_tokens_equivalent). Credit = min(CustomerMonthlyCommitment, floor(S / CT) * (MonthlyFee * 0.025)) with a per-incident cap equal to 10% of monthly committed spend. 4) Remediation Ladder: Notice -> 72-hour mitigation plan -> 7-day priority remediation -> if SLA missing persists beyond 14 days, customer may elect: (a) add credits as computed, (b) migrate traffic to alternate region with Redwood-assisted failover, or (c) terminate contract per termination schedule. 5) Autoscale Interlock: When autoscaler is in forced-throttle state, Redwood will pause further billing for throttled tokens and flag the event for remediation. 6) Force Majeure carve-outs and maintenance windows documented in Appendix B.
measurement_spec: Metrics (implemented by runtime telemetry): 1) CT_Attainment: 5-min sliding average of tokens served divided by committed tokens (expressed as %). Query window: 30-day rolling; aggregation: p99 of daily CT_Attainment. 2) Tail-Latency-Serve: 95th-percentile server-side end-to-end token latency when CT_Attainment < 95% (measured per 5-min intervals). 3) Sustained-Burst-Handling: fraction of burst windows (defined as >2x baseline request rate sustained for 60s) where observed throughput >= 75% of burst-equivalent capacity. Measurement rules: telemetry tags by customer_id, model_variant, region, and autoscale_state. Incident attribution: only intervals where Redwood infrastructure (not customer misconfiguration or upstream networking) is root cause will count toward shortfall. Data retention for SLA computations: 90 days.
rollout_notes: 1) Legal: review 2025-03-05. 2) Engineering: implement telemetry panels and a daily SLA computation job by 2025-03-10. 3) Finance: produce three example credit runs (small/mid/large accounts) by 2025-03-07. 4) Pilot: invite two existing Dedicated customers to opt-in pilot addendum; aim to collect pilot telemetry for 30 days. 5) Console: add 'Throughput Assurance' page with computed rolling attainment and upcoming remediation steps. 6) Documentation: FAQ and appendix for 'what counts as a shortfall' and sample calculations. 7) Go/No-Go criteria: automated metric computation validated against historical incidents and acceptance signoffs from Legal, Finance, and two pilot customers.
